cells.tense: The pattern sits open on the table and you are still looking at it.
cells.act: spend an hour with the thing you love without a task attached to it
cells.ask: Give an hour to the thing you love with nothing attached — nothing to finish, nothing to show, no use for it. And then simply stop. No tidying up after.
cells.core:
You can go deep into something and come back with the pattern intact. Others go in and come out with an answer; you come out with the shape underneath, and it holds where the answer would not. What you reach that way belongs to you, and it does not need defending.

Where that is working, you sketch the shape by hand — then start tidying it up before anyone has seen it. Give an hour to the thing you love this week and attach nothing to it: nothing to finish, nothing to show, no use for it. That is the depth settling instead of being explained. What is already held does not require an audience to exist, and the hour will end without anything having to come out of it.
cells.sheetLine: You go deep and come back holding the shape of it.
cells.verb: going so deep into a pattern that thought arrives at its own edge
cells.place: still walking toward a light you recognised but did not choose

cells.tense: The version that will finally land has not been drafted, and you are already braced.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Say the shape of what you are making — plainly, once, to someone — before they ask and before it is finished. Put the frame down and do not argue for it.
cells.core:
The pressure sits at the far end of what you are building. The finished version has already been drafted in your head, so the work on the desk keeps reading as provisional, and you keep deciding whether to speak until the later version arrives. The thinking has not gone soft. It has gone out past the work, deciding whether the work is allowed to count yet.

Where this is working, the frame is already sound — the shape of the thing could be handed over now and it would hold. Say it to someone before they ask, before it is done. A sketch spoken aloud has something solid to sit on; a sketch held back sits on the person holding it. Once the current piece is standing out in the open you can see what it is, not only what it will be.
cells.sheetLine: You are braced against a version of the work that has not arrived.

cells.tense: You stood under a light you did not pick, and you keep looking back at where it was.
cells.act: share the joy with the people it belongs to
cells.ask: Take one good thing from this week and say it out loud to the person it belongs to, while it is still warm — not in a day or two, not once you have earned it.
cells.core:
The direction you were walking in is behind you and the walking has stopped. You can still see it — that part was the easy part. From outside it reads as thinking; inside, it is a room you visit and will not work in. The pull has not been taken away. It has gone quiet, and quiet has become the habit.

Where this is working, direction returns through other people rather than through effort alone. Take one good thing that happened and say it aloud to the person it belongs to — not after, not in a day or two. Joy spoken with someone comes back with your own momentum in it: you hear your voice carry and remember where you were headed. Charge the room and the walking resumes. Push straight at the distant light and you will only stand there longer.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see the direction. You have stopped walking.

cells.tense: You are deep in something and calling it nothing much while you are.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Sit with some settled understanding about someone close to you — five quiet minutes, no deciding, no fixing, no account of it afterward.
cells.core:
Other people watch you get somewhere real with a hard question; later you describe the whole session as poking around. You go deep and come back with something that holds, and the account you give of your own life leaves the going out. What is happening is slow, earned understanding, and the name on it, when you offer one, is that it wasn't much.

Where this is working, you can sit with a settled understanding and do nothing with it — and you will not say so out loud. Sit with some settled understanding about someone close to you, five quiet minutes, no deciding and no fixing. Understanding held as understanding, not as a project, is where the depth stops being a secret. Try a second sitting and it will feel less like work than the first.
cells.sheetLine: What you call poking around is the understanding itself.
